description: Building SPHEREx-JARVIS, an interactive Solar System Scope-inspired web explorer and AI co-pilot for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. Our tool lets citizen scientists blink multi-epoch NASA infrared sky surveys (2MASS, AllWISE, and SPHEREx DR1), isolate fast-moving brown dwarfs and variable stars via image subtraction, and inspect 102-band near-infrared chemical spectra using voice or text commands.
summary:
PHEREx-JARVIS is a browser-based interactive sky-blink and spectral discovery console built for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. Using a Solar System Scope-inspired interface backed by NASA/IPAC IRSA SPHEREx Data Release 1 (DR1), AllWISE, and 2MASS parameters, our tool lets anyone enter Right Ascension and Declination coordinates—or select NASA’s five benchmark targets (WISE 0855, Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi B, RW Aurigae, and R Draconis)—to play multi-epoch time-lapse flipbooks that reveal moving brown dwarfs and variable stars.
To make citizen science accessible and accurate, we added an Image Subtraction Mode that suppresses static background stars, an interactive 102-band near-infrared spectrum graph (0.75–5.0 µm) highlighting water-ice and methane signatures, a SpaceX Starlink LEO Streak Guard to flag satellite contamination, and an adaptive voice/text JARVIS AI Co-Pilot with a Citizen Discovery Logbook. Because SPHEREx maps over a billion objects every six months, SPHEREx-JARVIS empowers everyday volunteers to spot hidden solar-system neighbors and share discoveries via one-click coordinate URLs.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:
SPHEREx-JARVIS is a browser-based, interactive sky-blink comparator and spectral discovery console inspired by Solar System Scope. Users enter custom Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) sky coordinates—or click quick presets for NASA’s five benchmark targets (WISE 0855, Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi B, RW Aurigae, and R Draconis)—to play multi-epoch time-lapse flipbooks (E1–E4) or manually scrub frame by frame. As epochs cycle, high-proper-motion brown dwarfs and variable stars visibly shift position or pulse in brightness inside an astrometric reticle while distant background stars remain fixed.

Key Features, Benefits & Intended Impact:

  • Image Subtraction ("Subtract Stars") Mode: Suppresses static background starlight so moving solar-system neighbors and transient anomalies stand out immediately in high-contrast crimson.
  • 102-Band Near-Infrared Spectral Profiler (0.75–5.0 µm): Visualizes SPHEREx spectral curves with molecular markers (J, H, K, L, M bands), helping volunteers identify water ice (H₂O), methane (CH₄), and carbon monoxide (CO) signatures on the fly.
  • SpaceX Starlink LEO Streak Guard: Addresses satellite contamination metadata by flagging low-Earth orbit shell crossings so citizen scientists do not confuse bright satellite trails with genuine Planet X or brown dwarf candidates.
  • JARVIS Voice & Text AI Co-Pilot + Discovery Logbook: Powered by the Web Speech API and browser localStorage, JARVIS lets anyone navigate sky coordinates hands-free, runs an automated guided tour, and allows volunteers to flag anomalies, attach observation notes, export JSON/CSV reports, and share exact coordinates via URL parameters.
  • Intended Impact: SPHEREx maps over a billion objects every six months. By lowering the technical barrier of astronomical FITS analysis into a guided, voice-assisted web app, SPHEREx-JARVIS empowers students and everyday volunteers worldwide to accelerate new astronomical discoveries.

Tools, Coding Languages & Data Used:

  • Frontend & Visualization: HTML5, CSS3, TypeScript/JavaScript, React/Vite, Canvas API, and interactive charting libraries, developed and deployed via Bolt.new and hosted open-source on GitHub.
  • AI & Browser APIs: Web Speech API (for voice commands and spoken briefings) and localStorage (for persistent target tracking and discovery logs).
  • Data & Astrometry Benchmarks: Built around NASA/IPAC IRSA SPHEREx Data Release 1 (DR1) (10.26131/IRSA678), AllWISE, and 2MASS infrared survey parameters alongside official CDS/NASA coordinates for WISE 0855 (RA 08h55m10.831s, Dec -07d14m42.53s), Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi B, RW Aurigae, and R Draconis.

Creativity & Design Factors Considered:
Rather than building a plain academic table, we designed a tactical, dark-space Solar System Scope-style Mission Control interface with a 3-Step Workflow Tracker (Target Set → Blink/Diff → Flag & Export). We specifically prioritized zero-install browser performance, false-positive prevention (via the Starlink Streak Guard), and accessibility for non-experts through JARVIS voice guidance and one-click shareable URLs
